dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?
Hi, yeah, it's still doing it. The water, it's still sitting there since the weekend, and now it's running down toward the garage next door. I don't even know who I'm supposed to call about this.
Okay, let me back up a little so I have it right. You're talking about water in the street, after the storm?
Right, the nor'easter, Friday and Saturday, two days ago. It's Monday and it's not draining. The drain by the corner is just full, like it's not taking anything.
Got it. And where are you, what's the address or the closest one?
Ninety-five Bliss Road. Easton's Beach side, you know, up toward the beach end.
Ninety-five Bliss Road. Okay. And the water you're seeing, is it right in front of your house or at the corner?

It's across the crosswalk. By the school bus stop. It's pooled all the way across, wide, and the kids are standing there in the morning and they can't get across without going in it, so they're stepping out into the road to go around. Into the road, with cars coming. I watched it this morning.
Oh, that's not good. So the crosswalk is underwater and the kids are walking out around it into the travel lane.

Yes. Exactly. And I called, well, I mean I've been meaning to call since Saturday, but I figured it'd go down. It hasn't. It's actually moving now, like there's a current toward my neighbor's garage. The door's at the bottom of the driveway and it's heading right at it.
Okay. Is it going into the garage yet, or just heading that way?
Not in yet. It's maybe, I don't know, ten feet off. But it's creeping. [pause] Sorry, hang on, I'm at the post office, I'm waiting for them to hand me a package, so it's a little loud in here.
No problem, take your time. I can hear it. Let me ask you, is the storm drain itself covered with leaves or debris, or does it just look full of water?
I mean, when I walked by there was a bunch of leaves and sticks piled on the grate. Like a wad of them. So maybe that's it? But I'm not going to stand in the road and pull them out.
No, please don't do that, definitely stay out of the road. So leaves on the grate at the corner near the bus stop. I'll write that down. Is it one drain or more than one?
The one at the corner. There might be another one down the block but I didn't see it, the water's too deep to see.

Okay. I'm going to put this in as a drain blockage with water over the crosswalk and a safety concern because of the bus stop. That gets looked at faster than a plain puddle complaint. Is it okay if I read back what I have?
Yeah, please.

Ninety-five Bliss Road, Easton's Beach side. Storm drain at the corner appears blocked with leaves, water pooled across the crosswalk by the school bus stop, children stepping into the road to get around, and water flowing toward a neighbor's garage. Did I get that right?
That's it. That's all of it. I just want somebody to come look at it today, honestly, before the buses come this afternoon.

I hear you. I'll mark it urgent for the crew. After a storm like that they've got a long list of drains, so I can't tell you the hour, but with the school stop involved it goes near the top. Do you want a call back when it's been cleared?
Sure. It's four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-seven-three.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-seven-three. And your name?
Carol Sherman.
Thank you, Carol. And is there anything the neighbor should do in the meantime about the garage?
I don't know. I guess I'll tell them. They're not home. Is there something they can put down? Sandbags, or whatever?

If they have any, those can help divert it. Otherwise just keep anything valuable off the garage floor. And if water actually starts coming in, call us back right away and say it's entering a building, and we'll bump it again.
Okay. I just, it's been two days. It seems like this drain always clogs up when it storms and nobody comes till somebody's yelling.
I understand. I'm noting that it's backed up for two days, too, so the crew sees how long it's been sitting. That helps.
Alright. They're calling my number here, I think. Hold on. [crosstalk] Yeah, that's me. Sorry, Lorraine, I've got to grab this.
Go ahead, get your package. You're all set on our end, and we'll call you when the crew's been out. Take care, Carol.
Thanks. Bye.
